thread:
harper: Heads up, discovered a late shard (s-91) that skipped a downstream window. Hourly aggregates for several customers are missing for 2024-07-10 00:00-06:00. Thinking targeted replay.
leo: Can we avoid re-ingesting everything? how narrow can we be?
harper: We have partition + tenant list + hour buckets. Rough numbers: ~450M events, mostly 2 tenants with heavy volume.
anjali: Two asks: a dry-run planner to estimate cost/duration and a console control to pin to backfill pool. Non-ops needs safe defaults.
miguel: Scheduler currently supports tags but no dry-run. We can add a planner endpoint that returns shards, worker count, token estimate, and an action checksum.
harper: Action checksum is important so console can show expected delta after replay for quick QA.
leo: Also need per-tenant rate caps. Last time a noisy tenant hogged workers and killed inference throughput.
anjali: Agree. Suggest per-tenant QPS cap and batch-size override in replay config. Console should surface both.
miguel: For routing, I propose a backfill affinity tag: affinity=backfill_pool. Backfill_pool has lower priority but reserved capacity so it never steals prod capacity.
harper: Nice. But what if reserved capacity is insufficient? need fallback policy: either queue or burst to preemptible nodes with soft-preempt.
leo: Soft-preempt semantics: backfills pause and persist checkpoints when a high-priority request needs the slot; resume after. This requires checkpointing at worker-level.
miguel: Checkpointing already exists for some jobs; we need to generalize to replay workers. Fairly straightforward: flush progress every N batches.
anjali: Can we have a dry-run in console that shows cost estimate and a confidence band? e.g., estimate 1.1k-1.6k compute tokens and 95% CI for duration.
harper: Yes. Planner could simulate processing rates using historical throughput on s-91 and build a distribution. Dry-run should return: shards_to_scan, estimated_rows, token_estimate, wall_time_estimate, cost_estimate_eur, confidence_pct.
leo: Also include a "safety knob" default: auto-limit to 30% of backfill_pool throughput and max 4 workers during rollout. Ops can lift later.
miguel: Implementation note: new API endpoints: POST /planner/dry_run -> {query} and POST /replay -> {plan_id} which references the plan from dry_run. That prevents accidental runs.
anjali: UI: disable direct "Start replay" unless user has a plan_id with a verified dry-run. Show clickable checkbox: "I understand the cost" + require role backfill-approver for unbounded runs.
harper: Also alerts: we need a flow to suppress SLO pages for a sanctioned backfill. Attach a run id to the alert mute window.
miguel: scheduler-bot: planner dry_run accepted. plan_id=pl_20240710_91_1 status: ready.
leo: I'll verify the plan and run a small canary (30m) against tenant xcorp. If canary passes, escalate with the safety knobs.
anjali: After this, I'll mock console preflight screen and show the plan_id, cost, duration, and "expected delta" checksum.
harper: Thanks. Please also add a small CSV report from canary validating aggregate diffs. That helps product verify correctness without diving into infra.
miguel: scheduler-bot: canary job 842 created referencing plan_id pl_20240710_91_1. status: queued.
leo: launching canary. will update.
anjali: Filing a short RFC for: planner dry-run API, plan_id gating, backfill_pool affinity, soft-preempt checkpoints, console preflight UI, and alert-mute integration.
harper: Great. Let's keep the default conservative. We can iterate once RFC lands.
miguel: scheduler-bot: canary job 842 running (1/1). ETA ~7m.
leo: Canary looks good. aggregates match expected checksums. Will scale with safety caps.
harper: Scaling now. tagging run with metadata: {scheduled_by:harper, run_reason:late_shard, plan_id:pl_20240710_91_1, alert_mute:true}.
jordan: (typo) — meant to say congrats, but not in thread.
miguel: scheduler-bot: replay job 843 started (2 workers, affinity=backfill_pool, preemptible=true).
anjali: Thanks team — I'll start mockups for the console preflight and share in #eng-ux next week.
harper: Filing follow-ups and postmortem on root cause. Thanks all.
